Commentary.Commentary: ...THE CHASE...

Later, the ever-reliable Beth Mooney managed to show her intent, as she scored a half-century towards the end to get their side to a fightable 247. But the day unquestionably belonged to Sarah Glenn, who was the undeniable pick of the bowlers, finishing with a magnificent five-wicket haul. Support came from Bell and Em Arlott who picked two wickets while Capsey chipped in with one. Now, the stage is set for a thrilling chase. Can England Women overcome their rivals and make a huge statement heading into the big event? We shall find out when the chase begins. Stay tuned!

The game, however, was dramatically flipped on its head by the brilliance of Sarah Glenn. Stepping up to deliver the 16th over, she dismissed both Ashleigh Gardner and Phoebe Litchfield in the same over. Litchfield departed after scoring 71. It then triggered the collapse of wickets, and from that moment on, the Australian middle-order crumbled under the pressure.

England Women, led by the wizardry of their spin attack, have bossed the first innings, restricting the mighty Australia Women to a competitive yet manageable 247 runs. The Aussies lost two quick wickets early on, but a composed and crucial partnership between the aggressive Phoebe Litchfield and the experienced Ashleigh Gardner steadied the ship. Litchfield took on the role of the aggressor, while Gardner played a vital second fiddle, anchoring the partnership of 82 runs for the third wicket.
